problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(1,0,3)$ and is parallel to the vectors ${v}_{1}=⟨5,2,1⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,3,3⟩.$

feedback.problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(1,-1,1)$, $P(2,0,3)$ and $Q(1,1,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,P$ and $Q$ are $a=⟨1,-1,1⟩,\,p=⟨2,0,3⟩,$ and $q=⟨1,1,0⟩.$

First, using the $3$ points we build $2$ vectors parallel to the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1} & =\overset{\to }{AP} \\  & =⟨2,0,3⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,2⟩ \\ {v}_{2} & =\overset{\to }{AQ} \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩-⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we need to find the normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={v}_{1}\times {v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+j+2k \\  & =⟨-5,1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =⟨2,0,3⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-5,1,2⟩ & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z & =-4 \\ -5x+y+2z+4 & =0 \\ 5x-y-2z-4 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
